npm publish preflight

Paste your package.json, your ignore files and your file list. Get the exact set of files npm publish would upload — and for every file, the one rule that decided it.

Runs entirely in this page. Nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere — your file list never leaves the browser. Every rule below is traceable to npm's own documentation; the sources are listed at the bottom.

Paste a file list and press Resolve — or load the example to see the classic accident.

The rules this page applies, and where each one comes from

Always included, whatever your files array or ignore files say: package.json, README and LICENSE/LICENCE at the package root in any case and any extension, the file named by main, and the file(s) named by bin.

Always ignored: *.orig, .*.swp, .DS_Store, ._*, .git, .hg, .lock-wscript, .npmrc, .svn, .wafpickle-*, CVS, config.gypi, node_modules, npm-debug.log, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, bun.lockb — plus .gitignore and .npmignore themselves.

Cannot be re-included even if you name them explicitly: .git, .npmrc, node_modules, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, bun.lockb.

.npmignore replaces .gitignore — it does not merge with it. If .npmignore is missing, .gitignore's contents are used instead. So an empty .npmignore is a real idiom: it turns .gitignore off entirely and publishes everything.

files[] currently wins over .npmignore. npm's own wiki says entries matched by files are included regardless of .npmignore — and flags that as its open issue #11669 rather than intended design. This page follows the documented behaviour and says so on every affected row.

Two places npm's docs are silent, and what this page does — named rather than resolved quietly:

  • Do npm's default ignores still apply inside a directory named by files? The docs are explicit only about the hard-core list. This page takes the conservative reading — they do apply — and labels any file it drops that way npm-default-ignore, so you can see it and disagree.
  • Are README/LICENSE honoured at any depth or only at the package root? The docs say "any case and extension" and nothing about depth. npm's own packlist anchors them to the root, so this page does too.

A pattern rule that is not about patterns: npm's walker never descends into an excluded directory, so a ! deeper in the file never gets to run. This page tests every ancestor directory and treats the first excluded one as final — which is why build/ followed by !build/keep.js still leaves build/keep.js out.

Sources. package.json → files · npm developers guide · npm/cli wiki: Files & Ignores · pattern syntax follows gitignore(5), which npm states its ignore files match.

What this is not. It is not npm pack --dry-run: it never reads your disk, never resolves bundleDependencies, and does not know about workspaces. It answers the question --dry-run does not — which rule decided this file. The credential alarm is this page's own heuristic on file names, not an npm rule, and it never changes a verdict.
